answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I see your notice in the gate of the community garden about the volunteer for the weekend and I want to help you. I am living in Fenton Street since three year, so the garden is very near from my house.

Firstly, I want to help because I like very much the plants and the green place. In my country my family have a small land and we grow there the tomato, the pepper and some flower. Here I have only a balcony and it is not the same thing. Also I don't know many people in this neighbourhood and in the garden maybe I can meet with new persons, this is good for me too.

Secondly, about my skill. I can dig, I can carry the heavy thing and I am not afraid from the hard work. I don't have a experience in the professional garden, but my mother learn me many thing when I was a child and I can learn fast the rest.

Thirdly, I can come in the weekend. Please tell me what I must to bring with me.

Thanks a lot,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: The first two points are addressed with real content (the reason is personal, the experience concrete), but the third point is left at I can come in the weekend: there is no day, no time, no duration, so the organiser cannot plan with this information. A formal application letter closes with Thanks a lot, so the register slips at the end of the letter.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly are stuck onto the points; Secondly, about my skill is not even a sentence and opens the paragraph. The sequence is trackable, but the links never go beyond and and also.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Words are everyday and repetitive: very much, good for me, many thing. Forms such as meet with new persons and afraid from the hard work stop the reader for a moment, though meaning is not lost.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: I see your notice (tense), since three year, my family have, we grow there, a experience, my mother learn me, I must to bring. Structures consist of simple sentences and sequences added with and/because.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Write the third point with a date and time: state which days, at what time, how many hours a week they could come. This single addition moves the task response up one band and gives the letter a real next step.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about the notice on the gate of the Fenton Street community garden, which is asking for volunteers at the weekends. I would like very much to join you.

I have lived in this street for three years and I pass the garden every morning on my way to the work. I would like to help for two reason. The first one is that I enjoy gardening but I only have a small balcony in my flat, so I have no place to grow anything. The second one is that I moved to this city recently and I would like to know my neighbours better.

About my experience, I grew up in a family who had a small piece of land, and I helped my parents with the vegetables and the fruit trees every summer. I am comfortable with digging, weeding and watering, and I can use most of hand tools. I have never worked in a public garden, but I am a quick learner and I don't mind the physical work.

I am free on Saturday mornings from nine o'clock until one o'clock, and I could also come on Sunday afternoon if you need more people at that time. Please let me know how I can register and if I should to bring my own gloves.

Yours faithfully,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are addressed and the third is given as a time range, with a registration question at the close. The experience section stays a little general: rather than how long a given task was done, it lists what they can do.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Paragraphs map onto the points properly, and The first one / The second one makes the internal structure clear. Transitions stay within topic-announcing patterns such as About my experience, with limited variety.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items suited to the task, such as weeding, quick learner, register, physical work, are correctly used, and the register stays that of an application letter throughout. In places such as most of hand tools and would like very much, the form does not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and a conditional clause are correctly used, and long sentences do not lose structure. The remaining errors (for two reason, a family who had, most of hand tools, if I should to bring) are visible but do not block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Make the experience concrete with an example (what was grown, how many years, what was done in which season), and clean up the plural/determiner errors; together these would pull up both the vocabulary and grammar scores.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing in response to the notice on the gate of the Fenton Street community garden, which invites volunteers to help with planting and with keeping the beds and paths in order at weekends. I would be glad to take part.

I have lived a few doors from the garden for three years and I walk past it every morning, so I have watched it change with the seasons without ever contributing anything to it. Two things attract me. The first is simply that I miss growing things: my flat has a north-facing balcony and nothing survives on it. The second is that I moved to the city as an adult and still know my neighbours only by sight, which a shared job outdoors would change faster than anything else I can think of.

As for what I can offer, I grew up helping my parents on a smallholding, where I was responsible for the vegetable beds every summer from planting to harvest. I am confident with digging, weeding, pruning and watering, and I have handled a strimmer and a rotary tiller. Public planting is new to me, but the work itself is not.

I could commit to Saturday mornings, from nine until one, and to alternate Sunday afternoons if there is a shortage of hands. Could you let me know how to register and whether tools are provided?

Yours faithfully,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are fully developed and each carries information the reader can use: the reason is split into two, the experience is described at the level of responsibility, and availability is tied to specific days and times. The two questions in the closing give the letter a real next step.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The letter follows the logic of an application: the advertisement, the reason, the qualification, the availability, the question. The structure opened with Two things attract me carries the next two sentences; links are built with reference words and structure rather than ready-made patterns.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as smallholding, from planting to harvest, alternate Sunday afternoons, shortage of hands appear with the right collocation. Choices such as know my neighbours only by sight sound natural; the register is formal but stays warm.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, participles and long non-inverted compound structures are controlled; punctuation is accurate. Errors are rare, though the long sentence in the second paragraph is a little crowded compared with the ease of band 9.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Split the long sentence in the second paragraph in two, and add a single figure to the experience section (how many years, how many square metres); the letter would become just as long but more precise.
